profile.name: Daniel Slaver MBENGUI
profile.tagline: Between Geneva and Luanda, I blend technology and creativity to bring projects to life.
profile.hudIntro: Passionate about code, I blend technology and creativity to bring your projects to life. Between tech and business, I'm your innovation partner!

birth.title: Birth
birth.description: I was born in February 1989 in Luanda, in the Palanca neighborhood, in Angola.

immigration.title: Stopover in Italy
immigration.description: Arrival in Italy with my mother and sister: a stopover in Como, a transit leg on the road to our new life, before continuing on to Switzerland.

asylum.title: Asylum application in Switzerland
asylum.description: After the stopover in Italy, my mother, my sister and I file our asylum application in Switzerland. June 1991 marks the start of our settlement and a new chapter on Swiss soil.

asylumDenied.title: Asylum application refused
asylumDenied.description: In September 1991, the Swiss authorities refuse our asylum application. A difficult turning point for my mother, my sister and me, with a future to rebuild amid uncertainty.

returnAngola1991.title: Return to Angola
returnAngola1991.description: After the asylum refusal, my mother, my sister and I return to Angola. Back to our home country to pick up our story and prepare for what comes next.

fatherSoloSwitzerland.title: My father sets off alone for Switzerland
fatherSoloSwitzerland.description: My father tries the adventure in Switzerland on his own, hoping to pave the way so we can join him later—while my mother, my sister and I wait in Angola.

fatherReturnAngola1992.title: My father returns to Angola
fatherReturnAngola1992.description: In April 1992, my father comes back to join us in Angola, with the same outcome as ours: his asylum application in Switzerland was refused too. The whole family is together again at home.

retrySwitzerland1992.title: We try again for Switzerland
retrySwitzerland1992.description: In August 1992, my mother, my sister and I set off again to try our luck in Switzerland—a new attempt after the 1991 refusals, hoping to build our future there.

flightToSwitzerland1992.title: Flying to Switzerland
flightToSwitzerland1992.description: Still August 1992: my mother, my sister and I are on the plane, heading for Switzerland. A moment in between—the Angola we leave and the welcome we hope for.

asylumAccepted1992.title: Asylum granted
asylumAccepted1992.description: In November 1992, Switzerland finally grants our asylum application—my mother, my sister and me. After the 1991 refusals and the long road through 1992, relief and the start of a lasting settlement.

foyerAccueil1992.title: Moving into a reception home
foyerAccueil1992.description: In December 1992, my mother, my sister and I move into a reception home. Our first concrete steps into everyday life in Switzerland—support, new people, and learning the country that has taken us in.

fatherJoinsFoyer1993.title: My father joins us at the home
fatherJoinsFoyer1993.description: In March 1993, my father finally joins us at the reception home in Switzerland. The family is together again: after the separations and attempts of 1991–1992, we share our new daily life under one roof.

apartmentGeneva1993.title: Moving into a new apartment
apartmentGeneva1993.description: In May 1993, we leave the reception home and move into a new apartment in Geneva. A place of our own at last, where the whole family settles in and starts putting down roots.

parentsWorkingStable.title: My parents back at work
parentsWorkingStable.description: In July 1993, my father and mother each find work in Geneva. We are truly settled: an apartment, steady incomes—our lives finally settle into a calm routine.

schoolEntry1993.title: Starting school
schoolEntry1993.description: In September 1993, my sister and I start school in Geneva. Our first steps into the Swiss education system—new classrooms, classmates, and French every day.

peacefulLifeGeneva.title: A peaceful life in Geneva
peacefulLifeGeneva.description: From the 1993 school year through November 1996, we live a normal, peaceful life in Geneva. The whole family adapts to local culture; French becomes our everyday language—at school, at work, with neighbors—and our Swiss roots grow stronger.

avanchets1996.title: Moving to Les Avanchets
avanchets1996.description: In December 1996, we move to the Les Avanchets neighborhood, still in Geneva. A new home, a new community—the family keeps putting down roots in the city that welcomed us.

primarySchoolAvanchets1997.title: Starting primary school
primarySchoolAvanchets1997.description: In January 1997, my sister and I start primary school in Les Avanchets. The neighborhood school, classmates nearby—our education finally fits the place we call home.

footballClubAvanchets.title: Neighborhood club football
footballClubAvanchets.description: From August 1998 to June 2001, I play football at the neighborhood club in Les Avanchets. Training, matches, and teammates—my first years of team sport, rooted in local community life.

coudriers2001.title: Starting orientation cycle
coudriers2001.description: In September 2001, I start the orientation cycle at Les Coudriers in Geneva. A new school stage—broader subjects, guidance, and preparing the choices ahead in my education.

collegeRousseau2004.title: Starting at Collège Rousseau
collegeRousseau2004.description: In September 2004, I start lower secondary at Collège Rousseau in Geneva. Higher expectations, new subjects, and a school setting that shapes the next stage of my education.

schneider.title: Internship at Schneider & Cie SA
schneider.description: In August 2008, I take a turn into the semi-professional world and start my internship at Schneider & Cie SA—freight transport, combined with the Madame De Staël business school.

jeunesseco.title: Founding Jeunesse&Co
jeunesseco.description: In November 2009, I help create the Jeunesse&Co association and, on that occasion, write my first article—published in Actu Vernier about the birth of the project and youth engagement in the neighborhood.

actu2010.title: Jeunesse&Co's first event
actu2010.description: In February 2010, Jeunesse&Co holds its first official evening—a milestone for the association and the neighborhood. I cover it in a second article published in Actu Vernier.

cfc.title: Federal VET Diploma in Commerce
cfc.description: In June 2011, I earn my Federal Certificate of Competence as a commercial employee—the culmination of three years of work-study at Schneider & Cie and the Madame De Staël business school.

itopie2013.title: Internship at Itopie
itopie2013.description: From January to April 2013, I intern at Itopie to explore the IT world. The experience convinces me to pursue this field and change direction once again.

esig.title: Joining ESIG
esig.description: In September 2013, I start at the School of Business IT (ESIG) in Geneva—following through on my new direction after the Itopie internship and the real start of my IT path.

esigSideJobs.title: Student jobs during ESIG
esigSideJobs.description: While studying at ESIG, from 2013 through late 2014, I take on various part-time jobs: tuition was free but brought in no income, and I wanted earnings on the side—to treat myself on weekends, among other things.

esigDiploma2015.title: ESIG diploma
esigDiploma2015.description: In June 2015, I earn my Federal Diploma in Business IT from ESIG—two years of training that cement my move into the IT profession.

imad2015.title: Internship then job at IMAD
imad2015.description: From February to June 2015, I complete my internship at IMAD; from June to August 2015, I stay on as an administrative employee—including setting up a CMDB to inventory the company's IT assets.

heg2015.title: Starting at HEG
heg2015.description: From September 2015 to February 2016, I start at the University of Applied Sciences in Business Administration (HEG) in Geneva. I leave the program mid-year—other ideas were already pulling me elsewhere.

backToAngola.title: Back to Angola & M. Dandela
backToAngola.description: From June to August 2016, I return to Angola alongside my father to help create M. Dandela—the family business (cybercafé, real estate) that marks my adult ties to the country.

ifage.title: Ifage certificate: JEE & Android
ifage.description: From September 2018 to March 2019, I train at Ifage and earn the JEE & Android Developer certificate—discovering Android Studio and the Ionic framework.

pythonScrum.title: Python & Scrum
pythonScrum.description: From July to October 2019: Python certificate at IT Training Academy and Professional Scrum Master I training.

javaSe11.title: Java SE11 during the pandemic
javaSe11.description: From February to March 2020, Java SE11 training started on-site and finished via video conference as Covid-19 began.

fccResponsive2022.title: Responsive Web Design · freeCodeCamp
fccResponsive2022.description: In March 2022, I earn the freeCodeCamp Responsive Web Design certification—HTML, CSS, and adaptive layout.

fccJavascript2022.title: JavaScript Algorithms · freeCodeCamp
fccJavascript2022.description: In March 2022, I complete the freeCodeCamp JavaScript Algorithms and Data Structures certification.

winno.title: Winno Bearz Club
winno.description: From April to July 2022, the Winno Bearz Club project—a collection of 5,555 generative NFTs with over 194 traits, listed on OpenSea.

fortytwoPiscine2022.title: The Piscine · 42 Lausanne
fortytwoPiscine2022.description: In August 2022, the Piscine at 42 Lausanne—the intensive bootcamp leading to admission: projects, peer learning, and full immersion in 42 culture.

alphaBusinessCentre.title: Office at Alpha Business Centre
alphaBusinessCentre.description: In September 2022, setting up my office at Alpha Business Centre—a workspace to structure my projects before and during my return to study.

fortytwo.title: Starting at 42 Lausanne
fortytwo.description: In September 2022, I joined the curriculum at 42 Lausanne: team-based projects and a gamified path—PlayPad and Dandela Academy both started as ideas during this time.

drilldev.title: Drill Dev
drilldev.description: From February to April 2023, a mandatory project at 42 Lausanne: I built the Drill Dev website to showcase AI image generation—mainly Midjourney—and related tools and workflows.

playpadIdea.title: The PlayPad idea
playpadIdea.description: In May 2023, the PlayPad idea took shape with Omar, Jonathan, and Joel—finding padel partners and organizing games became the core of the project.

playpadLaunch.title: PlayPad launch
playpadLaunch.description: In November 2023, the PlayPad app launched—first public release to connect players and streamline bookings.

playpadSarl.title: PlayPad Sàrl
playpadSarl.description: In April 2024, PlayPad Sàrl was officially founded—the legal structure for the entrepreneurial venture around the app.

playpadPartners.title: PlayPad partners
playpadPartners.description: In May 2024, Airpad and GVA Padel joined the PlayPad venture—new partners to grow Geneva's padel ecosystem around the app.

dandela.title: The Dandela Academy idea
dandela.description: In September 2024, the Dandela Academy idea took shape with my father—a vocational training school in Luanda—and construction work on the building got underway.

fortytwoBlackHole.title: Black Hole · leaving 42 Lausanne
fortytwoBlackHole.description: In November 2024, my time at 42 Lausanne ended. In the Common Core, the “Black Hole” is a deadline that moves forward as you validate projects and earn XP—if you haven't progressed enough in time, you “fall in” and can no longer continue the program. With PlayPad and Dandela Academy pulling my focus, I didn't push that limit far enough: the end of my 42 journey.

playpadHack.title: PlayPad hacked
playpadHack.description: In December 2024, our PlayPad app was hacked. We immediately lost both partners—Airpad and GVA Padel. The team was devastated—a brutal blow to the venture.

xaiInterview.title: xAI interview
xaiInterview.description: In January 2025, after PlayPad, a one-hour conversation with xAI teams: presenting my profile and clearing the path to technical assessments.

react.title: React certification · back in the game
react.description: From February to March 2025, I got back into development: intensive practice and the Front-End Engineering with React certification (CodeSignal), ready for xAI's challenges.

xaiTechnicalTests.title: xAI technical tests
xaiTechnicalTests.description: From April to May 2025, three demanding xAI technical tests—algorithms, coding, and real-world scenarios—at the heart of the hiring process.

xaiResults.title: xAI results
xaiResults.description: In June 2025, the results arrived: a final rejection, but not a bitter one—I had reached the last stage of the process. A formative experience that affirmed my tech path.

dandelaInefop.title: Official founding · Dandela Academy
dandelaInefop.description: In July 2025, official creation of Dandela Academy and registration with INEFOP (Instituto Nacional de Emprego e Formação Profissional)—Angola's public body overseeing employment and certified vocational training.

playpadRelaunch.title: PlayPad relaunch
playpadRelaunch.description: In September 2025, we relaunched the PlayPad app—back to square one, without partners. What matters is holding to our convictions; new allies will come if we stay true to the vision.

dandelaTeam.title: Dandela Academy team
dandelaTeam.description: In January 2026, building the teaching and operations team for Dandela Academy—the people to carry the school and its digital platform.

dandelaOpening.title: Dandela Academy opening
dandelaOpening.description: In February 2026, the official opening of Dandela Academy—a certified vocational school with a digital platform and AI at the heart of learning.

playpadVps.title: PlayPad · new release
playpadVps.description: In September 2026, a new, much smoother PlayPad release—hosted on our own VPS to regain control, especially on security after the 2024 hack.

vaakaiStore.title: Vaakai Store
vaakaiStore.description: In October 2026, launch of the Vaakai Store website—a Swiss online grocery with catalog, loyalty, and multilingual UX, built with Dandela Tech.

today.title: Today · developer & entrepreneur
today.description: From Angola to Geneva—a path of setbacks that teach and wins that keep you moving: business CFC, ESIG diploma, tech pivots, 42 Lausanne, PlayPad (hack, relaunches, VPS), xAI challenge, Dandela Academy with my father. Today I'm a Full Stack & Mobile developer and entrepreneur—commerce, code, and impact, with AI as a daily lever.
